injective really got its staking etf listed on nasdaq before gta 6 came out. 😭

on november 5, canary capital launched the canary staked inj etf ($injc) on nasdaq, bringing @injective's native asset directly into traditional financial markets.

this news is particularly interesting because of the staking component. unlike a regular spot etf, $injc provides exposure to inj while allowing the fund to participate in network staking. any rewards earned can contribute to the fund's value after fees and expenses.

for traditional investors, this means gaining exposure to injective through ordinary brokerage accounts without managing crypto wallets, private keys, or validators.

the timing couldn't be more interesting. injective has been expanding its institutional infrastructure, from its sec-registered transfer agent initiative to the recently introduced institutional rail, designed to improve how financial institutions interact with the blockchain.

now, with $injc trading on nasdaq, another connection between injective and wall street has been established. whether significant institutional capital follows remains to be seen, but the accessibility and visibility this creates are worth recognizing.

a few years ago, seeing a staking-enabled investment product tied to injective on a major american stock exchange would have sounded ambitious. today, it's a reality.

and somehow, we're still waiting for gta 6.

US mortgage demand is down to historic lows:

US purchase mortgage applications index fell -2% last week, to 131 points, its 2nd-lowest since January 2025.

This also marks the 6th-lowest weekly reading since 1995, down -32% since January.

As a result, US mortgage applications are now -50% below the pre-pandemic levels seen in 2019.

This comes as the 30Y fixed mortgage rate has risen +120 basis points since February, to 7.18%, near its highest since November 2023.

Rates have now been above 7.0% for 7 consecutive weeks.

The US housing market is frozen.
